assumption_note: Geologic DACCS has comparatively clear mass-balance and storage monitoring logic, but still needs buffers for measurement, leakage, and invalidated credits.
Weathering credit depends on reaction verification, transport, counterfactual baselines, runoff chemistry, and regional environmental constraints.
Ocean alkalinity has large theoretical potential but open-ocean mixing, ecological risk, counterfactuals, and attribution make crediting harder than contained storage.
BECCS has durable geologic storage if captured, but biomass supply, land-use accounting, lifecycle emissions, and storage monitoring must all clear.
Biochar credit depends on feedstock, process conditions, product fate, soil/material application, and durability over decades to centuries.
Land biological storage is important for climate and ecosystems, but fire, drought, land-use change, counterfactuals, and non-permanence make 100-year crediting fragile.
